Co-optimization of multiple virtual power plants considering 
electricity-heat-carbon trading: A Stackelberg game strategy

Stackelberg game 
Carbon trading 
Demand response 
Kriging metamodel 
ABSTRACT  
With the improvement of the electricity-heat-carbon trading mechanism, it has been a trend for multiple virtual 
power plants (MVPP) to participate in the market competition. Firstly, in order to mitigate the burden of 
environmental pollution and balance the conflicting market interests of MVPP, this paper proposes a Stackelberg 
game strategy for the operator and MVPP considering a ladder-type carbon price mechanism and a dual- 
compensated demand response (DR) mechanism, which consists of an optimal pricing strategy for the oper -
ator and an optimal energy scheduling strategy for each VPP. During the game process, the operator serves as the 
leader, guiding the energy transactions of MVPP through price optimization, while each VPP acts as the follower, 
optimizing the internal aggregated units and loads based on the price issued. To solve the Stackelberg game 
equilibrium, a Kriging metamodel is then adopted to fit the energy scheduling model of the VPP. Finally, several 
cases are analyzed to verify that the proposed strategy can effectively contribute to the energy complementation 
and carbon reduction of MVPP.   
1. Introduction 
With the development of distributed energy resources (DER), the 
energy structure of the world is gradually shifting from the centralized 
utilization of large-scale fossil energy to the distributed usage of multi- 
type energy resources, which will greatly relieve the pressures on energy 
exploitation and environmental protection [1] . However, due to the 
small capacity and fluctuating power output of DERs, their large-scale 
grid connection will pose a series of safety problems. To address the 
challenge, a virtual power plant (VPP) aggregating DERs, energy storage 
equipment, and loads is developed, which breaks the limits of 
geographic location and resource type [2] . As an integrated entity, the 
VPP can carry out energy dispatch and market trading independently, 
providing an effective solution to the large-scale grid connection and 
rational consumption of DERs [3] . 
Currently, the energy scheduling strategy for a VPP in the context of 
the market transaction is a hot topic of research. Reference [4] proposed 
a combined approach for interval and deterministic optimization to 
solve the VPP scheduling problem. Reference [5] explored a two-stage 
optimal VPP operational mechanism considering the reserve uncer -
tainty, which includes a novel day-ahead offering strategy and a real- 
time dispatching model. Reference [6] established a VPP optimal 
scheduling model of energy sharing and interaction among various re -
gions, and the model is solved by the compound differential evolution 
algorithm. Reference [7] proposed a multi-timescale VPP scheduling 
scheme, including a scenario-based robust optimization for the day- 
ahead scheduling and two receding horizon optimizations for the 
close-to-real-time dispatch. With the development of the electricity- 
heat-carbon trading mechanism, multiple VPPs (MVPP) combining en -
ergy production and consumption gradually compete in the market [8] . 
Driven by the market transaction prices, each VPP, as an independent 
stakeholder, tends to pursue its maximum interest. Therefore, the cur -
rent investigated methods for optimizing the scheduling of a single VPP 
are not applicable to the optimization of MVPP. 
In general, the fundamental issue required to be solved for the 
collaborative optimal scheduling of MVPP is the description of the 
interaction behavior between the different stakeholders. Game theory is 
a common method for studying the equilibrium of interests between 
multiple agents, which is widely used in the economic field [9] . At 
present, many researchers focus on using game theory to solve the 
optimal scheduling problems of various market participants. In refer -
ence [10] , the advertising differential game is introduced to depict the 
competition among electricity operators in continuous time. In reference

[11] , a market mechanism for real-time reactive power ancillary service 
market based on the Stackelberg game model is proposed considering 
voltage-apparent power coupled subsystems. In reference [12] , the 
interaction between consumers and the operator is modeled as a 
Stackelberg game to analyze the impact of real-time electricity. By 
analyzing the game objectives and strategies of the multi-agent system, 
the unique Stackelberg equilibrium solution of the hierarchical Stack -
elberg game is proved theoretically in reference [13] . To study the 
regulatory performance of the dynamic electricity price mechanism 
adopted by the power operator, a non-cooperative Stackelberg model is 
constructed based on game theory in reference [14] . These studies have 
confirmed that the theory plays an important role in power trading to 
address the interaction of interests between MVPP. However, current 
studies mainly focus on operator-led electricity stakeholders and rarely 
consider entities with multi-energy coupling properties. Hence, the 
MVPP game considering electrothermal coupling and multi-energy 
trading is required to be studied in depth. 
As the game theory involves a multi-layer model optimization, the 
solution of the game model of MVPP can be converted into a large-scale 
optimization problem for complex systems [15] . Generally speaking, the 
heuristic intelligence algorithm and the analytical approach based on 
Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions are the two main methods for 
solving the game equilibrium solution. The heuristic intelligent algo -
rithm involves frequent calls to models, which will reduce the solving 
speed [16] . Whereas the analytical approach based on KKT conditions 
requires the invocation of all parameter information, which will pose 
privacy issues [17] . In addition, KKT conditions are suitable for seeking 
the optimal solution of a convex optimization problem, which imposes a 
convexity requirement on the objective function and constraints of the 
model [18] . To address these problems, it is essential to simplify the 
complex game model. Due to the good fitting and error estimation 
capability for non-linear models, the Kriging metamodel is used as an 
approximate alternative to the complicated model [19] . Referring to the 
successful application of the Kriging metamodel in the optimal power 
flow problem solving [20] and the economic dispatch problem solving 
considering the wind uncertainty [21] , it would be introduced to reduce 
the difficulty of the game equilibrium solution solving. Moreover, as the 
fit accuracy of the metamodel directly affects the game results, a 
correction mechanism of the Kriging metamodel should be further 
researched to improve the fitting ability. 
With the development of the carbon market, carbon trading is 
considered to be an essential tool for balancing the environment and 
economy [22] . Researches on the carbon trading of the VPP are ongoing. 
Based on the optimization of cooling, heating, and electricity load and 
the ladder-type carbon trading mechanism, reference [23] established 
an optimal scheduling model with a carbon capture device. Reference 
[24] introduced a carbon trading mechanism and a carbon emission 
calculation model and proposed an optimal scheduling strategy for a 
VPP considering the carbon trading cost. Reference [6] incorporated the 
cost of carbon trading into the economic operation model of a VPP with 
carbon capture equipment and analyzed the impact of carbon trading 
prices on the VPP operation. Reference [25] explored a ladder-type 
carbon trading mechanism and studied the impact of a ladder-type 
carbon price on system operation profits and carbon emissions. Based 
on the life cycle assessment for the energy chains, the normalized carbon 
emission coefficient and the ladder-type carbon trading mechanism 
considering the reward and punishment are adopted in reference [26] to 
calculate the carbon trading cost. Reference [27] examined factors 
affecting carbon pricing, including environmental, social, political, and 
economic variables. Existing research on carbon trading concentrate on 
the innovation of transaction mechanisms, the tracking of carbon foot -
prints, and the analysis of pricing influences, exploring the impact of 
carbon trading on systemic carbon emissions and operating costs. 
However, the current studies mainly investigate a single VPP and rarely 
examine the joint carbon trading of MVPP, especially the impact of 
energy interactions between MVPP on carbon trading. 
To manage the load distribution within the VPP, a demand response 
(DR) mechanism is commonly adopted to compensate the energy con -
sumers for reducing or transferring the loads during peak hours of en -
ergy usage [28] . Existing researches focus on analyzing the impact of DR 
on costs and load distributions. Reference [29] suggested that imple -
menting DR would decrease the total operating costs of VPP. Reference 
[30] indicated that the DR scheme induced more load reductions, which 
mitigated critical load and decreased VPP operation costs. Reference 
[31] indicated that the price-based DR could realize peak load shifting, 
and the incentive-based DR could reduce the operation cost. In reference 
[32] , the energy and reserve scheduling with and without DR partici -
pants is addressed in detail via comparison. As a component of the VPP 
dispatch strategy, a sequential DR scheme was proposed in reference 
[33] to reduce both ramping rate and peak power at the aggregated 
level. Reference [34] reduced the penalty costs in day-ahead and real- 
time scheduling through the balance of spinning reserves with DR ser -
vices. However, few studies examine the impact of DR on the carbon 
trading of the VPP from the load side. Moreover, current researches on 
DR are relatively simple, with a single compensation mechanism, and 
the impact of DR on the carbon emissions of MVPP is rarely analyzed. 
In response to the above issues, this paper proposes a Stackelberg 
game strategy for the operator and MVPP considering a ladder-type 
carbon price mechanism and a dual-compensated DR mechanism, 
which consists of an optimal pricing strategy for the operator and an 
optimal energy scheduling strategy for the VPP. To solve the Stackelberg 
game equilibrium solution, a corrected Kriging metamodel is adopted. 
The main contributions of this paper are summarized as follows.  
(1) Considering the electrothermal coupling for MVPP, a Stackelberg 
game model is developed to coordinate the energy transactions 
between the operator and MVPP, which will be beneficial for 
energy consumption and the complementation of VPP.  
(2) To improve the ability of the Kriging metamodel to fit the MVPP 
model, this paper proposes a dynamic update algorithm of sam -
pling points to correct the Kriging metamodel.  
(3) Based on a ladder-type carbon price mechanism, the impact of 
MVPP energy interactions driven by the Stackelberg game on 
carbon trading is researched, and the carbon reduction potential 
is further explored.  
(4) Unlike the traditional DR mechanism with a single price 
compensation, this paper establishes a dual-compensated DR 
mechanism considering the energy price compensation and the 
carbon subsidy and investigates the contribution of DR to carbon 
emission reduction.

The remainder of the paper is organized as follows: Section 2 in -
troduces the operational characteristics of the operator and MVPP, 
including the Stackelberg game structure, the framework of the ladder- 
type carbon price mechanism, and the framework of the dual- 
compensated DR mechanism. Section 3 establishes mathematic models 
of the operator and MVPP including objective functions and constraints, 
and proves the Nash equilibrium of the Stackelberg game model. Section 
4 introduces the solving method for the established model. The case 
study and result analysis are presented in section 5 . Section 6 draws the 
conclusion. 
2. Operational characteristics for the operator and MVPP 
In this paper, the VPP consists of wind turbines (WT), photovoltaics 
(PV), gas turbines (GT), waste heat recovery boilers (WHRB), heat ex -
changers (HE), gas boilers (GB), energy storage systems (ESS), and dis -
patchable loads (DL), so as to coordinate the cleanliness of renewable 
energy generation and the controllability of fossil energy supply. Among 
them, on the basis of the electrical and thermal consumption demands 
from the energy users, the DL can be further divided into the dis -
patchable electric loads (DEL) and the dispatchable heating loads (DHL). 
In addition, the GT, WHRB, and HE comprise a combined heat and 
power (CHP) supply device. While the GT is generating electricity, the 
heat in the discharged cooling water and flue gas can be recycled 
through the WHRB, and together with the heat generated by the GB, the 
combined heat can be supplied to users through the HE. 
Due to the profit-driven nature of market conditions and different 
characteristics of resource endowments, the internal energy supply, and 
energy consumption are often unbalanced for each VPP, which presents 
energy shortages or energy surpluses during some periods. Conse -
quently, an operator is introduced in this paper to coordinate the 
complementarity of the unbalanced energy resources among MVPP. 
Drawing on the mechanism of the European electricity market operation 
[35] , the structure of MVPP and the operator is illustrated in Fig. 1 . As 
shown in Fig. 1 , each VPP, as an independent entity, reasonably arranges 
its internal resource scheduling under the electricity and heat trading 
price issued by the operator, as well as the forecast information of load 
and renewable energy, and carries out the transaction of the shortfall or 
surplus energy with the operator. Acting as an intermediary, the oper -
ator on the distribution side aggregates energy trading information from 
MVPP and then makes the difference by centralizing the purchase and 
sale of electricity in the electricity market at the power grid tariff and 
feed-in tariff. In addition, both the operator and MVPP participate in the 
carbon market transaction simultaneously. 
2.1. The Stackelberg game structure 
For the energy trading process between the operator and MVPP, the 
operator prioritizes issuing the pricing strategy based on the energy 
demand of each VPP, and the VPP then formulates the energy scheduling 
strategy under the guidance of the price signal. On the contrary, the 
energy dispatch decisions of MVPP will affect the energy transactions 
with the operator, which can in turn lead to the adjustment in the pricing 
decision of the operator. The energy trading process between the oper -
ator and MVPP is sequential and interactive, which is in line with the 
dynamic game of master – slave recursive structure, so the Stackelberg 
game is adopted in this paper to analyze the interaction between the 
stakeholders. 
In general, the participants, strategies, and objective functions are 
the three basic elements of a game model, and the framework of the 
Stackelberg game is illustrated in Fig. 2 . As shown in Fig. 2 , the operator 
and MVPP act as participants, taking on the roles of the leader and 
followers respectively during the process of Stackelberg game. Driven by 
the objective functions of maximizing the operator ’ s profit and mini -
mizing the VPP operating cost, the corresponding game strategies are 
formulated, which can be divided into the pricing strategy for the 
operator and the energy scheduling strategy for each VPP. The pricing 
strategy involves the purchase and sale prices for the electricity and heat

2.2. Framework of the ladder-type carbon price mechanism 
Considering the operating guidelines of the Chinese carbon market, 
the free carbon emission allowances (CEA) are allocated to each carbon 
emission source through a baseline method, the allocation basis of 
which is distinguished by the electrical and thermal energy. In general, 
when the actual carbon emission is lower than the allocated allowance, 
the remaining allowance can be sold in the carbon trading market, and 
conversely, it is required to be purchased. In this paper, the energy 
production from the CHP and GB within MVPP, and the upper grid 
power purchase by the operator constitute the main sources of carbon 
emissions. The process of carbon trading involving a coupled electricity- 
heat-carbon relationship is illustrated in Fig. 3 . 
Contrary to traditional carbon trading with a fixed carbon price, the 
ladder-type pricing mechanism considering the reward and punishment 
is developed in this paper for the enthusiasm of the carbon reduction and 
the constraint on carbon emission. According to the mechanism, several 
CEA purchase and sale bands are divided, and as a penalty, the carbon 
price for the corresponding interval rises by a certain percentage with 
the increase of the CEA volume to be purchased. Similarly, the excess 
CEA can be sold under different sale bands with proportionally 
increasing reward prices. Therefore, for the operator and MVPP, the 
carbon trading cost based on the ladder-type carbon price mechanism is

2.3. Framework of the dual-compensated DR mechanism 
In order to guide energy consumers within the VPP to transfer or 
reduce part of their loads during peak hours of electricity and heat 
usage, the DR program for electric and thermal loads is applied in this 
paper, which can be divided into incentive-based demand response 
(IDR) and price-based demand response (PDR). According to the two 
dispatch forms of DR, the DEL and DHL can be further divided into the

electric load (IEL), and interruptible heat load (IHL). To be more spe -
cific, the SEL and SHL allow for spontaneous load shifting in response to 
price fluctuations, whereas the IEL and IHL reduce their loads with the 
incentive issued by the VPP. 
Due to the interactivity of the energy supply and consumption in the 
VPP, the adjustment of energy use strategies under the DR will also in -
fluence the output scheme of the energy supply equipment, thus 
affecting the carbon trading of the VPP. Therefore, considering the 
coupling of electricity, heat, and carbon emissions, this paper proposes a 
dual compensation mechanism for the DEL and DHL that combines the 
energy price compensation and the carbon subsidy, so as to investigate 
the impact of load regulation capability on the energy dispatch and 
carbon emissions. Generally speaking, in order to guide users to actively 
reduce energy consumption and adjust energy use periods during peak 
load hours, energy compensation prices for SEL, SHL, IEL, and IHL are 
set respectively by the VPP. Then, based on CEA coefficients for unit 
electricity and heat, the curtailment volume of electric and thermal 
loads in response to compensation prices are converted into carbon 
emission reductions, which are dually compensated in the form of car -
bon subsidies according to the benchmark carbon price.

3. Stackelberg game model for the operator and MVPP 
In this paper, the Stackelberg game model includes the upper-layer 
optimal pricing model for the operator and the lower-layer optimal 
energy scheduling model for the VPP. The optimal dispatch problem of 
the operator and MVPP can be described as the optimization of two-

into the following three aspects. a) The set of strategies of participants 
and followers is a non-empty tight convex set. b) There exists a unique 
optimal solution for all followers when the strategy of the leader is 
given. c) There exists a unique optimal solution for the leader when the 
strategies of followers are given. 
According to the above three conditions, the existence and unique -
ness of the Stackelberg equilibrium for the game model developed in this 
paper are proved as follows. a) From the model of the game participants, 
it can be seen that the strategy of the operator is required to satisfy the 
constraint (10) , and the strategies of MVPP are restricted by constraint 
(18)-(28). Therefore, the strategy set of each participant is non-empty 
and tightly convex. b) The objective function of the VPP consists of 
four components. Among them, the cost functions for energy purchase 
and sale, DR compensation, and carbon trading are quasi-convex due to 
their linear characteristics. The cost function for the internal unit 
operation is non-linear, however, it is also quasi-convex as the quadratic 
term coefficients are positive. Thus, for given energy trading prices from 
the operator, the objective functions of MVPP are quasi-convex, and the 
unique optimal solution within the scope of the VPP strategy set exists. 
c) From formula (3) – (7), it is clear that the objective function of the 
operator is linear and quasi-convex. Therefore, for the energy scheduling 
strategy finalized by each VPP, the optimal energy trading prices 
determined by the operator within its strategy set are unique. In a 
nutshell, there exists a unique Nash equilibrium solution in the Stack -
elberg game model developed in this paper. 
4. Stackelberg game solving based on the Kriging metamodel 
algorithm 
As the lower-layer VPP optimal scheduling model established in this 
paper contains 0 – 1 variables, the optimization of the lower-layer model

Stackelberg game that each VPP develops the energy trading scheme

relationship between the trading price and the trading volume, and the 
mapping relationship in this paper is fitted by developing a computa -

4.2. Dynamic correction of the Kriging metamodel 
The accuracy of the Stackelberg game solution depends on the 
Kriging model fit, which is directly influenced by the number of sample 
points, and excessive sample points can reduce the speed of the solution. 
In order to determine the proper number of sample points, this paper 
proposes a dynamic update algorithm of sampling points to modify the 
Kriging metamodel. Based on the initial Kriging model, the function 
values of the upper-layer pricing model can be derived. The strategy set 
in the upper layer is divided into multiple subsets according to the 
function values, thus eliminating the space of the strategy set containing 
a low probability of global optimal solutions and reducing the dynamic 
update range of sampling points. The strategy set division method is 
specified in Appendix B. For each strategy subset, the upper-layer model 
is solved with the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to obtain 
the locally optimal energy trading prices determined by the operator, 
and the lower-layer scheduling model is invoked to solve the corre -
sponding locally optimal energy trading volume. Then, the solved 
locally optimal energy trading prices and volumes are added to the 
initial sample dataset, and the initial Kriging metamodel is modified to 
obtain the equilibrium solution of the Stackelberg game through 
iterations. 
Based on the initial development and dynamic correction of the 
Kriging metamodel, the Stackelberg game model-solving process with 
the Kriging metamodel is shown in Fig. 5 , and the detailed procedures 
are as follows.  
a) Input parameters for the operator and MVPP.  
b) Sample points for energy trading prices are generated based on the 
LHS, and the volume of energy traded for each VPP is solved by 
invoking the lower-layer energy scheduling model.  
c) Generate the initial sample dataset, and develop the initial Kriging 
metamodel to replace the lower layer model.  
d) Calculate the value of the objective function corresponding to each 
sample dataset, divide the strategy set into z subsets accordingly, and 
solve the locally optimal energy trading prices of each subset space 
with the PSO algorithm.  
e) Invoke the lower-layer model to solve the corresponding locally 
optimal energy trading volume and add them to the initial sample 
dataset.  
f) Based on the updated sample dataset, the initial Kriging metamodel 
is corrected, and the optimal function value of the upper-layer model 
in each subset is calculated.  
g) Compare the optimal function values in all subsets and take the 
maximum value as the global optimal solution for the current 
iteration.  
h) Determine whether the global optimal solutions of the two iterations 
are equal, if not, continue iterating, otherwise output the final result.

6. Conclusion 
Based on a ladder-type carbon price mechanism for carbon trading 
and a dual compensation mechanism for DR, this paper develops a multi- 
stakeholder Stackelberg game strategy with the operator as the leader 
and VPPs as followers. Considering the multi-energy coupling charac -
teristic, the strategy realizes the optimal low-carbon and economic 
scheduling for the operator and VPPs. Multiple cases are set up for 
comparative analysis, and the conclusions are as follows. 
a) In the Stackelberg game model, the pricing strategy from the oper -
ator guides MVPP to dispatch internal resources and carry out energy 
trading rationally, while the energy purchase and sale decisions for 
MVPP will in turn influence the setting of energy prices. With the 
optimization of energy prices, the Stackelberg game strategy facili -
tates the internal energy exchange between VPPs, which further 
promotes energy consumption within the VPP and coordinates the 
complementarity of energy resources from other VPPs. As a result, 
the total cost of a VPP can be reduced by up to 13.89 %, while the 
profit of the operator is increased by 11.07 %.
